meta.titre: Unicellular Organisms: Amoeba, Chlamydomonas and Yeast Compared with Spirogyra
meta.sous_theme: Single-celled organisms and the green alga Spirogyra

sections.contenu_markdown:
A drop of water taken from a pond near a village may look clean to the eye, yet under a microscope it can hold tiny living things that swim, creep or float.
Some of them are whole organisms made of one cell, and one cell must do every job that a whole body does in a goat or a human.
GCE Biology often asks you to name the structures of these organisms, to say what a structure does, or to compare one organism with another.
This course gives you the facts and the method to answer each type of question.

items: A cell has a cell membrane, cytoplasm and a nucleus; a plant cell also has a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large vacuole.
Photosynthesis is the way green plants and algae make food using light and chlorophyll.
Osmosis is the movement of water through a partially permeable membrane from a dilute solution to a more concentrated one.

sections.contenu_markdown:
### Unicellular means one cell
A **unicellular organism** is a whole living thing made of a single cell. That one cell feeds, respires, gets rid of waste, moves, grows, reproduces and responds to its surroundings.

### Four organisms compared

| Feature | Amoeba | Chlamydomonas | Yeast | Spirogyra |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of cells | One | One | One | Many, joined end to end in a filament |
| Cell wall | Absent | Present | Present | Present (cellulose) |
| Chloroplast | Absent | One cup-shaped chloroplast | Absent | Spiral ribbon-shaped chloroplasts |
| Pyrenoids | Absent | Present | Absent | Present |
| Movement | Pseudopodia | Two flagella | None | None |
| Nutrition | Feeds on other organisms | Makes its own food | Feeds on sugars and other organic matter | Makes its own food |
| Contractile vacuole | Present | Present | Absent | Absent |
| Reproduction | Binary fission | Cell division | Budding | Fragmentation or conjugation |

### Amoeba in detail
Amoeba has no fixed shape. It pushes out **pseudopodia** (false feet) to move and to surround food. The food is enclosed in a **food vacuole**, where enzymes digest it. An Amoeba living in fresh water is surrounded by a dilute liquid, so water enters its cell by osmosis; the **contractile vacuole** collects this extra water and expels it (**osmoregulation**). Amoeba has no cell wall and no chloroplast.

### Green organisms
A **pyrenoid** is a small body in the chloroplast linked with starch storage. Chloroplasts with pyrenoids point to a green alga such as Chlamydomonas or Spirogyra, never to Amoeba or yeast.

variantes.nom: Naming an organism from its parts
variantes.quand_utiliser: When a list of structures is given and one organism must be chosen
variantes.contenu_markdown: Start with the rare structure. A chloroplast rules out Amoeba and yeast. A pyrenoid confirms a green alga. A contractile vacuole points to Amoeba or Chlamydomonas, not to yeast or Spirogyra. Cross out every organism that lacks one listed part.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question says compare, differentiate or how is X different from Y
variantes.contenu_markdown: Write each difference as a pair in one sentence: 'Spirogyra has a cell wall, but Amoeba has none.' A feature for one organism alone earns no mark. Choose features that really differ: cell wall, chloroplasts, movement, nutrition.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a magnification is given and the real size is asked
variantes.contenu_markdown: $$\text{actual size} = \frac{\text{size in the drawing}}{\text{magnification}}$$ Use the same unit for both lengths. One millimetre is 1000 micrometres.

sections.enonce_markdown: Compare Chlamydomonas with Amoeba by giving **four** differences. *(4 marks)*

etapes.justification: 'Compare' needs a point on each organism in every sentence, not a list for one.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Each answer has two halves: Chlamydomonas and Amoeba.

etapes.justification: Good choices are structures that are present in one organism and absent in the other, and ways of feeding and moving.

etapes.action: Write each pair in one sentence.
etapes.justification: A sentence with 'but' or 'whereas' shows both sides at once.
etapes.resultat_markdown: See the table in the conclusion.

etapes.action: Check that the four pairs are different ideas.
etapes.justification: Each mark is for a separate idea, so two pairs about the same structure would earn one mark only.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Cell wall, chloroplast, movement and nutrition are four separate ideas.

sections.conclusion_markdown:
| Chlamydomonas | Amoeba |
|---|---|
| Has a cell wall | Has no cell wall |
| Has a chloroplast (with a pyrenoid) | Has no chloroplast |
| Moves with two flagella | Moves with pseudopodia |
| Makes its own food by photosynthesis | Takes in food and digests it in food vacuoles |

items.pourquoi_faux: Spirogyra grows as a long thread in which many cells are joined end to end.
items.correction_markdown: Spirogyra is a multicellular filament; each cell has its own wall, chloroplast and nucleus.

items.erreur_markdown: Amoeba has chloroplasts, so it makes its own food.
items.pourquoi_faux: Amoeba has no chloroplast and no cell wall; it must take in other organisms or food particles.
items.correction_markdown: Amoeba is a consumer that engulfs food with pseudopodia.

items.erreur_markdown: The contractile vacuole digests the food in Amoeba.
items.pourquoi_faux: Digestion takes place in the food vacuole. The contractile vacuole removes excess water.
items.correction_markdown: Food vacuole: digestion. Contractile vacuole: osmoregulation.

items.pourquoi_faux: Flagella are whip-like threads, as in Chlamydomonas. Amoeba flows forward by pushing out parts of its cytoplasm.
items.correction_markdown: Amoeba uses pseudopodia; Chlamydomonas uses two flagella.

items.erreur_markdown: Spirogyra: has a cell wall. Amoeba: moves.
items.pourquoi_faux: The two features do not belong to the same property, so the examiner cannot see a difference.
items.correction_markdown: Compare the same property: 'Spirogyra has a cell wall, but Amoeba has none.'

items.enonce_markdown:
(a) Name the structure with which Amoeba surrounds a food particle.

(b) Name the structure in which the food is then digested.

(c) Name the structure that removes extra water.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) **Pseudopodia** (false feet) flow around the particle.

(b) The **food vacuole**; enzymes pass into it and digest the food.

(c) The **contractile vacuole**.

items.enonce_markdown:
Copy and complete the table with 'yes' or 'no'.

| Organism | Cell wall | Chloroplast | Flagellum | Nucleus |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Amoeba | | | | |
| Chlamydomonas | | | | |
| Yeast | | | | |

A drawing of a yeast cell is 12 mm long at a magnification of 400. Calculate the actual length in micrometres.
items.solution_markdown:
| Organism | Cell wall | Chloroplast | Flagellum | Nucleus |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Amoeba | no | no | no | yes |
| Chlamydomonas | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| Yeast | yes | no | no | yes |

Actual length = 12 mm / 400 = 0.03 mm.

0.03 mm x 1000 = **30 micrometres**.

items.enonce_markdown:
A freshwater Amoeba is watched under a microscope. Its contractile vacuole fills and empties again and again.

(a) Explain why water keeps entering the Amoeba.

(b) The Amoeba is moved to a more concentrated solution. Predict what happens to the activity of the contractile vacuole, and explain.

(c) A drawing of this Amoeba is 45 mm long at a magnification of 300. Calculate the actual length in micrometres.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) The cytoplasm is more concentrated than the pond water, and the cell membrane is partially permeable, so water enters by **osmosis**.

(b) Less water enters because the solution outside is more concentrated, so the vacuole fills and empties **more slowly** and there is less water to remove.

(c) 45 mm / 300 = 0.15 mm; 0.15 x 1000 = **150 micrometres**.

items_markdown: A unicellular organism is a whole organism made of one cell that carries out all life processes.
Amoeba: pseudopodia for movement and feeding, food vacuoles for digestion, contractile vacuole for removing excess water; no cell wall and no chloroplast.
Chlamydomonas is a single green cell with a chloroplast, pyrenoid, two flagella and a cell wall.
Spirogyra is a green filament of many cells; its chloroplasts are spiral ribbons with pyrenoids.
In a comparison question, write both organisms in each sentence and compare the same feature.
Actual size = size in the drawing divided by the magnification.
